- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33), model underestimates; apply upward bias correction.
- After sharp price spikes (forecast > true outcome by >1.5x), model often overshoots; reduce forecast by 20–40% in next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; force mean reversion toward recent 7-day average.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is below 1.0x historical mean, model often overreacts; cap forecast at 1.5x recent 14-day average.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating ±0.67), model exhibits erratic behavior; smooth forecast with weighted average of last 5–7 days.
